description: Sézanne is Tokyo's most internationally visible contemporary French table, combining precise French technique with Japanese seasonality and a polished hotel dining experience. The Four Seasons setting, deep champagne program and current global ranking make it a first-call reservation for affluent visitors.
highlights: Three-star French tasting menu, global 50 Best recognition, Andre Fu interiors and luxury hotel service.
sources: Michelin Guide; The World's 50 Best Restaurants; Asia's 50 Best Restaurants; Four Seasons Hotel Tokyo at Marunouchi
hotel_name_hint: Four Seasons Hotel Tokyo at Marunouchi

description: Yoshihiro Narisawa's restaurant remains one of Tokyo's defining modern Japanese fine-dining addresses. Its satoyama philosophy, polished bilingual service and long international track record make it an essential bridge between Japanese terroir and global gastronomy.
highlights: Satoyama-inspired tasting menu, strong sustainability narrative and enduring global 50 Best status.
sources: Michelin Guide; The World's 50 Best Restaurants; Asia's 50 Best Restaurants; Condé Nast Traveler

description: Sazenka is a rare three-star Chinese restaurant in Tokyo, set in an elegant Minami-Azabu residence. Tomoya Kawada's cuisine fuses Chinese technique, Japanese seasonality and a refined tea-led sensibility into one of the city's most distinctive luxury dining experiences.
highlights: Three-star Japanese-Chinese cuisine in a former diplomat residence with rare tea and wine pairings.
sources: Michelin Guide; Asia's 50 Best Restaurants; The World's 50 Best Restaurants; Tabelog

description: L'Effervescence is one of Tokyo's most graceful modern French restaurants, balancing high culinary ambition with warmth and a quietly luxurious dining room. Shinobu Namae's cuisine is prized for its intellectual clarity, Japanese produce and elegant sense of hospitality.
highlights: Three-star modern French cuisine with a Japanese produce focus and serene Nishiazabu atmosphere.
sources: Michelin Guide; Tabelog; World of Mouth; Condé Nast Traveler

description: Quintessence is a benchmark for contemporary French cooking in Tokyo, defined by exacting technique, product-driven menus and an almost monastic focus on balance. It remains a serious destination for diners who value culinary purity over spectacle.
highlights: Three-star contemporary French tasting menu with rigorous technique and a cult reputation.
sources: Michelin Guide; Tabelog; World of Mouth; Tableall

description: RyuGin remains one of Tokyo's grand modern kaiseki flagships, now housed above Hibiya in a polished dining room designed for occasion dining. Seiji Yamamoto's cooking is theatrical, technical and deeply rooted in Japanese seasonal symbolism.
highlights: Three-star modern kaiseki, Hibiya skyline location and one of Japan's best-known chef-led dining rooms.
sources: Michelin Guide; Tabelog; World's 50 Best Discovery; World of Mouth

description: Kagurazaka Ishikawa is a discreet three-star kaiseki house tucked into one of Tokyo's most atmospheric old entertainment districts. The restaurant combines seasonal Japanese cooking, beautiful tableware and a level of hospitality that feels deeply personal.
highlights: Three-star kaiseki in Kagurazaka with intimate service and refined seasonal cooking.
sources: Michelin Guide; Eater; Tabelog; Tableall

description: Hiroyuki Kanda's restaurant is a long-running pillar of Tokyo kaiseki, now in Toranomon Hills with a contemporary stage for its refined seasonal cuisine. The experience is luxurious but controlled, with a careful dialogue between chef, guest, sake and ingredient.
highlights: Three-star kaiseki at Toranomon Hills with deep sake culture and elite concierge demand.
sources: Michelin Guide; Kanda official site; Tabelog; Tableall

description: Harutaka is one of Tokyo's most coveted Edo-style sushi counters, prized for exacting rice, pristine seafood and a restrained, ryokan-like atmosphere. It is a high-concentration experience for diners who want sushi at Tokyo's most serious luxury level.
highlights: Three-star Ginza sushi counter led by Harutaka Takahashi, with elite omakase craftsmanship.
sources: Michelin Guide; Tabelog; Tableall; OMAKASE

description: Joël Robuchon in Ebisu offers Tokyo's grandest expression of French haute cuisine, served inside a chateau-like dining room built for formal occasions. It remains a classic power reservation for affluent diners who want luxury, polish and a deep French wine program.
highlights: Three-star French haute cuisine in the landmark Ebisu chateau with grand service and cellar depth.
sources: Michelin Guide; Joël Robuchon official site; Tabelog; La Liste

description: Shiseido's L'Osier is one of Tokyo's great French dining rooms, combining haute cuisine, museum-level polish and a glamorous Ginza address. The atmosphere is sophisticated and international, with service and wine standards that suit formal business or celebratory dining.
highlights: Three-star Ginza French restaurant with dramatic interiors, luxury service and a serious cellar.
sources: Michelin Guide; Shiseido L'Osier; Tabelog; Elite Traveler

description: Myojaku rose quickly into Tokyo's top tier with a pure, restrained style of Japanese cuisine built around harmony, water and pristine seasonal ingredients. The minimalist Nishiazabu setting and chef-counter format make it feel both quiet and intensely special.
highlights: New three-star Japanese counter restaurant with Asia 50 Best recognition and minimalist design.
sources: Michelin Guide; Asia's 50 Best Restaurants; Myojaku official site; Tableall

description: Azabu Kadowaki is a luxurious kappo restaurant in Azabu-Juban known for seasonal omakase and a more expressive register of Japanese cuisine. It is especially relevant for affluent diners who want three-star cooking in a polished but intimate room.
highlights: Three-star kappo with seasonal omakase, truffle signatures and hotel-concierge reservation demand.
sources: Michelin Guide; Azabu Kadowaki official site; Tabelog; Condé Nast Traveler

description: Florilège brings Hiroyasu Kawate's vegetable-forward, French-Japanese tasting menu into the design-conscious setting of Azabudai Hills. It is one of Tokyo's most important contemporary restaurants, blending sustainability, theatre and a polished social atmosphere.
highlights: Two-star French-Japanese tasting menu, Azabudai Hills design setting and global 50 Best recognition.
sources: Michelin Guide; The World's 50 Best Restaurants; Asia's 50 Best Restaurants; Florilège official site

description: Matsukawa is a discreet, invitation-only kaiseki restaurant that sits at the very top of Japan's luxury dining conversation. Its near-mythic reservation difficulty, impeccable seasonal product and La Liste recognition make it unavoidable for a Tokyo affluent dining set.
highlights: Invitation-only kaiseki, La Liste top-tier recognition and one of Tokyo's most coveted counters.
sources: La Liste; 50 Best Discovery; Tabelog; Tableall

description: Den remains one of Tokyo's most beloved modern Japanese restaurants, famous for balancing serious technique with warmth, wit and emotional hospitality. It is less austere than many top Tokyo rooms, yet still delivers a deeply considered tasting menu.
highlights: Two-star modern Japanese tasting menu with playful hospitality and long 50 Best history.
sources: Michelin Guide; The World's 50 Best Restaurants; Asia's 50 Best Restaurants; World of Mouth

description: Crony is a polished Higashi-Azabu restaurant where French technique, Nordic restraint and Japanese sourcing meet in a warmly modern room. The restaurant's name signals its hospitality style: precise, refined and intentionally personal rather than formal for formality's sake.
highlights: Two-star modern French restaurant with Asia 50 Best recognition and a relaxed Scandinavian-influenced room.
sources: Michelin Guide; Asia's 50 Best Restaurants; Crony official site; Tabelog

description: MAZ translates the biodiversity research of Peru's Central into a Tokyo tasting menu built around altitude, ecosystems and Japanese ingredients. Its Kioicho location and conceptual clarity make it one of the city's strongest international fine-dining alternatives.
highlights: Two-star Peruvian-Japanese tasting menu, Asia 50 Best recognition and immersive altitude narrative.
sources: Michelin Guide; Asia's 50 Best Restaurants; MAZ official site; Tabelog

description: Ginza Shinohara delivers lavish, seasonal Japanese cuisine with a sense of occasion that appeals strongly to Tokyo gourmets. The room is discreet, but the cooking has a dramatic quality, especially in its ornate hassun and prized seasonal ingredients.
highlights: Two-star Ginza kaiseki known for lavish seasonal presentations and deep domestic gourmet following.
sources: Michelin Guide; Tabelog; OMAKASE; Foodies Reserve

description: Ginza Kojyu is a refined kaiseki counter that has long represented Tokyo's formal Japanese dining tradition. Its compact room, private spaces and deep beverage program make it a natural choice for affluent diners seeking classic Ginza hospitality.
highlights: Two-star Ginza kaiseki with private rooms, wine and sake depth and classic hospitality.
sources: Michelin Guide; Ginza Kojyu official site; Tabelog; Tableall

description: Nishiazabu Sushi Shin is one of Tokyo's benchmark traditional sushi counters, newly elevated to two Michelin stars in the 2026 guide. It retains the quiet, intimate feel of a neighborhood sushi room while serving seafood and rice at a rarefied level.
highlights: Two-star Nishiazabu sushi counter with long Michelin history and classic Edomae restraint.
sources: Michelin Guide; Sushi Shin official site; byFood; Tabelog

description: Hakuun is a modern Japanese counter in Minami-Aoyama, promoted to two stars in the 2026 Michelin selection. The cooking emphasizes dashi, fragrance, temperature and a flexible approach to classic Japanese cuisine.
highlights: Two-star Japanese counter with chef's-table format and a distinctive dashi-centered style.
sources: Michelin Guide; Hakuun official site; Tabelog; Tableall

description: Ensui is a two-star Naka-Meguro restaurant built around the elemental dialogue of flame and water. Dashi, charcoal and seasonal Japanese ingredients shape a deeply personal course menu in a softly lit counter setting.
highlights: Two-star Japanese restaurant in Naka-Meguro with dashi, charcoal and seasonal stew signatures.
sources: Michelin Guide; Tabelog; Tableall; En Primeur Club

description: ESqUISSE is one of Ginza's most polished French fine-dining restaurants, pairing a formal urban dining room with contemporary technique and Japanese product sensitivity. It remains a strong luxury alternative for business dinners and special occasions.
highlights: Two-star Ginza French restaurant with formal service, serious wine and polished urban luxury.
sources: Michelin Guide; ESqUISSE official site; Tabelog; World of Mouth

description: Tempura Kondo is a definitive luxury tempura counter in Ginza, known for the clarity of its batter, careful oil work and seasonal vegetables. The restaurant is an essential Tokyo counter experience for diners who want a single craft taken to its highest level.
highlights: Two-star tempura counter in Ginza, famous for precise frying and seasonal vegetable tempura.
sources: Michelin Guide; Tempura Kondo official site; Tabelog; World of Mouth

description: Sushi Kanesaka offers one of Ginza's classic luxury omakase experiences, with a restrained counter, pristine seafood and a style that has influenced high-end sushi beyond Japan. It is a polished option for diners seeking canonical Edomae sushi.
highlights: Two-star Ginza sushi counter with classic Edomae technique and an international reputation.
sources: Michelin Guide; Sushi Kanesaka official site; Tabelog; 50 Best Discovery

description: The Roppongi branch of Sukiyabashi Jiro carries one of Japan's most famous sushi names in a more accessible luxury setting than the original Ginza counter. It remains a serious Michelin-starred omakase for diners seeking the Jiro lineage.
highlights: Two-star Roppongi sushi counter with direct Jiro heritage and formal omakase service.
sources: Michelin Guide; Sukiyabashi Jiro official site; Tabelog; Tableall

description: Seizan is a highly regarded Mita restaurant that honors Japanese culinary tradition while allowing the menu to move with the seasons and the chef's point of view. It brings two-star cooking into a room that feels polished yet less theatrical than Tokyo's grandest kaiseki houses.
highlights: Two-star Japanese cuisine in Mita with seasonal courses and a strong domestic gourmet reputation.
sources: Michelin Guide; Seizan official site; Tabelog; OMAKASE

description: Ryuzu is a mature Roppongi French restaurant known for refined technique, balanced sauces and a calm, adult dining room. It is a reliable choice for affluent diners who want two-star French cooking without the grandeur of Tokyo's palace-style dining rooms.
highlights: Two-star Roppongi French restaurant with polished service and quietly luxurious atmosphere.
sources: Michelin Guide; Ryuzu official site; Tabelog; World of Mouth

description: Hommage gives Asakusa a serious modern French destination with a neighborhood warmth rare at this level. Noboru Arai's cooking is elegant and personal, and the location gives the restaurant a strong sense of Tokyo beyond the usual Ginza-Aoyama luxury circuit.
highlights: Two-star Asakusa French restaurant with personal cooking and a warm neighborhood setting.
sources: Michelin Guide; Hommage official site; Tabelog; World of Mouth

description: Ginza Kyubey is a classic sushi institution that remains deeply useful for affluent visitors who want a polished but less rarefied alternative to Tokyo's hardest-to-book counters. The service style is welcoming, the address is iconic and the experience feels culturally essential without being austere.
highlights: Classic Ginza sushi institution with counter theatre, polished service and strong visitor appeal.
sources: Tabelog; Condé Nast Traveler; Time Out Tokyo; World of Mouth

description: Sarashina Horii is a centuries-old soba house in Moto-Azabu, celebrated for its pale sarashina noodles and enduring place in Tokyo food culture. It is relaxed enough for a casual evening, but the history and craft make it rewarding for sophisticated diners.
highlights: Historic soba institution with more than two centuries of local reputation and classic duck soba options.
sources: Time Out Tokyo; Tabelog; Eater; Sarashina Horii official site

description: Suegen is a Shinbashi chicken kappo with roots dating back to the early twentieth century. Its dinner course centered on poultry hot pot gives affluent diners a relaxed but meaningful way into Tokyo's heritage dining culture.
highlights: Long-running Shinbashi chicken kappo with dinner courses, hot pot and old Tokyo atmosphere.
sources: Time Out Tokyo; Tabelog; Tokyo restaurant guides

description: Nihonbashi Otako Honten is a beloved oden specialist whose clear Kanto-style broth has made it a Tokyo winter and sake-drinking classic. The restaurant is informal, but its history, central location and focused kitchen give it strong cultural relevance.
highlights: Historic Nihonbashi oden house with long-simmered broth, sake and classic tomeshi.
sources: Time Out Tokyo; Tabelog; Tokyo heritage restaurant guides

description: Yamariki Honkan is a shitamachi institution in Morishita, famous for nikomi stew and yakiton in a lively, adult dining room. It is not a luxury restaurant, but it gives well-traveled diners a memorable taste of Tokyo's everyday culinary depth.
highlights: Century-old Morishita favorite for nikomi, yakiton, sake and a lively downtown atmosphere.
sources: Eater; Time Out Tokyo; Tabelog; Yamariki official site
